correct_completion: everyone left the office before six.
full_sentence: The meeting having finished early, everyone left the office before six.
acceptable_variants: and people went home well before six.
so everyone could leave the office early.

options.text: so everyone left the office before six.
options.why_wrong: 'So' is a linker that starts a new clause; an absolute clause must not be followed by a conjunction of this kind.

options.text: everyone left the office before six.
the everyone left the office before six.
options.why_wrong: 'The' cannot precede the pronoun 'everyone', so the main clause is ungrammatical.

options.text: everyone to leave the office before six.
options.why_wrong: An infinitive cannot serve as the main clause after an absolute construction, which needs a finite verb.

grammar_focus: Absolute (nominative absolute) clauses with a subject and a participle, followed by a main clause
explanation: An absolute clause has its own subject ('the meeting') and a participle ('having finished'), and it is separated from the main clause by a comma. It does not take a conjunction. Learners whose first language is Russian may add a linker because Russian allows more flexible clause joining, so English needs the comma structure without a connector.
translation: Когда совещание закончилось раньше времени, все покинули офис до шести.
